title: adaptive-prefetch-coalescer-and-headroom-prober: reduce long-tail latency under interleaved workloads
author: Ethan Li
description: Motivation: our multi-sequence interleaved workload traces exposed recurring p95/p99 spikes when concurrent sessions caused fragmented KV cache priming. This PR introduces two complementary components to improve steady-state tail latency and to measure headroom: 1) Adaptive Prefetch Coalescer: a lightweight runtime probe that detects small, temporally clustered key lookups across concurrent requests and issues aggregated prefetches for likely KV entries. Prefetch aggressiveness is controlled by an adaptive heuristic that tracks hit-rate delta and backoff on miss amplification. 2) Headroom Prober: a background sampler that injects low-overhead synthetic sequences under production-like concurrency to estimate remaining CPU/GPU headroom and identify noisy neighbors. Changes: - new runtime module benchmark_lab/prefetch/coalescer.go and coalescer tests - headroom prober harness under benchmark_lab/probers/headroom_prober.py with CLI + config - telemetry wiring: metrics and events exported to observability-pack (prefetch.attempts, prefetch.success_rate, prober.headroom_estimate, prober.latency_impact) - small API change in the session replayer to expose lookahead hints for prefetch (opt-in, off by default) - integration harness changes to include the prober in nightly long-tail runs Backwards compatibility: prefetch is opt-in via config; default behavior unchanged. Testing and results: ran the representative interleaved-seq workload (1000 concurrent sessions, mean seq len=210) in the lab. Compared against baseline nightly harness: p50 unchanged (~24ms), p95 reduced from 168ms to 132ms (-21%), p99 reduced from 312ms to 248ms (-21%). End-to-end throughput impact negligible (<1%). The prober adds ~0.3% extra token throughput load when enabled; metric collection overhead is <0.1%. Checklist: [x] unit tests for coalescer heuristics, [x] integration test with kvcache checkpointing, [x] perf run and report attached, [x] telemetry docs updated, [ ] roll-out gating config (follow-up ticket). Related: references ENG-4123 for KV cache regression, follows patterns from earlier adaptive prefetch experiments. Notes for reviewers: focus on correctness/edge cases in coalescer backoff logic (avoid thrashing) and on the prober sampling cadence (defaults tuned conservatively). Long-term: propose adding a canary flag to enable aggressive prefetch for dedicated capacity clusters. Attachments: perf CSVs and flamegraphs stored in run-2026-02-21 artifacts.

review_conversation: Maya Patel: Nice approach. Two quick asks: tighten the backoff math to avoid oscillation and add a stress test that forces repeated misses.
Ethan Li: Thanks Maya — tightened backoff coefficients and added a deterministic miss stress test in coalescer_test.go. See commit 3.
Zoe Chen: Telemetry looks good. Can we add a prometheus label for cluster_mode (hosted/dedicated) so we can slice results?
Ethan Li: Added cluster_mode label to prefetch metrics and updated the README. Also updated e2e to assert label presence.
Carlos Ruiz: Observed a flaky CI integration test on a re-run; appears resource-timing dependent. Suggest lowering timing sensitivity in the test harness.
Ethan Li: Made the test timing window wider and added retries for CI. Re-ran perf suite locally before pushing.
release_notes: Introduce adaptive prefetch coalescer to reduce long-tail latency for interleaved sequence workloads and add a headroom prober to estimate runtime capacity; opt-in via config; improves p95/p99 ~21% in lab runs.
notes_for_ops: Prefetch disabled by default. To enable in staging: set benchmarks.prefetch.enabled=true and tune benchmarks.prefetch.max_lookahead per cluster. Headroom prober should be scheduled during off-peak windows; default sampling rate is conservative.
